sections.title: Red flags
sections.alert: Red flag present. Hot swollen joint: treat as septic arthritis, aspirate before any antibiotic and arrange same-day orthopaedic or rheumatology review. Suspected giant cell arteritis: start high-dose glucocorticoids at once without waiting for results and refer the same day; visual symptoms need same-day ophthalmology review. Vasculitic rash with organ involvement: same-day specialist referral. Fever, sore throat or bruising on a DMARD: full blood count the same day.

advice.title: Staying safe on DMARD medicines
advice.text: Have your blood tests done on the dates given and bring your monitoring record to every visit. Contact the clinic at once if you get a sore throat, fever or other infection, mouth ulcers, unexplained bruising or bleeding, yellow eyes, or a new cough or breathlessness. Do not start or stop any medicine, including herbal remedies, without asking, and tell us before planning a pregnancy.

advice.title: Living with gout
advice.text: Take the urate-lowering tablets every day, even when you have no pain. Attacks can happen more often in the first few months; this does not mean the medicine is failing, so do not stop it. Cut down on alcohol, especially beer, on sugary drinks, and on red meat and seafood, and lose weight if you are overweight.

advice.title: When to come at once
advice.text: Come to hospital the same day if a joint suddenly becomes hot, swollen and very painful, especially with fever or if you take medicines that lower immunity. If you are over 50 and get a new headache, pain in the jaw when chewing, a tender scalp, or any loss or blurring of vision or double vision, come at once: this can cause blindness if not treated quickly.
